[MUQATIL:43:8-10/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | If Muhammad asks the Meccan unbelievers who created the heavens and earth, they answer that the Mighty in dominion and Knowing of His creation created them.
[TAB-FULL:v20p554/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | If asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists would answer that the mighty in power and vengeance, all-knowing of them and everything in them, created them.
[THALABI:v8p328/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | If asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists acknowledge the mighty, knowing Creator.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · صاحب النظم | reports | The author of al-Naẓm says the speech shifts from the unbelievers' reported answer to God's own description; otherwise they would say “for us,” not “for you.” The two attributes still describe the same God.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says Muhammad's people would acknowledge that the Mighty, Knowing God created the heavens and earth, affirming His justice and knowledge of creation.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi calls this confession a form of faith, though they contradict it by worshiping idols alongside God.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل المعاني | reports | The scholars of meaning call this the height of ignorance: they acknowledge God as creator, then associate others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p14/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | After finishing the report of their answer, God begins describing Himself in the following verse.
[DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Faith can refer to professing God while remaining in shirk; the People of the Book also accept some scripture while rejecting other parts and the messengers.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p206#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Muhammad's people admit that God, the Mighty and Knowing, created the heavens and earth, yet worship others and deny resurrection through extreme ignorance.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The pagans attribute creation of the heavens and earth to the one described as Mighty and Knowing.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The words We revived a dead land and the descriptions following the pagans’ admission are God’s speech, not theirs.
[TABRISI:43:6-10/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Muhammad's people must admit that God created the heavens and earth; He is almighty and knows creatures' interests.
[TABRISI:43:6-10/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Their admission that God created the heavens and earth exposes their ignorance: they then worship others with Him and deny His power to resurrect.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p303#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Their admission that God created the heavens and earth followed by worship of others exposes their ignorance, as the next verse continues the argument. | mentions 43:10
[RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | The question could be directed to prophets or unbelievers, but the nearer antecedent is the unbelievers, who admit God created the heavens, earth, and what lies between them.
[RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The point is that, despite admitting God is the creator, the polytheists worship others beside Him and deny His power to resurrect.
[RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The first divine attribute is creation of the heavens and earth; theologians make the world's origination and God's agency the first proof of God, with “created” understood as bringing into being.
[RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-ʿAzīz means overpowering; the capacity for dominance comes from power, so the name signals perfect power.
[RAZI-FULL:v27p168#2/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-ʿAlīm signals perfect knowledge; together, God's complete knowledge and power mean He can create every possible thing, after which the passage details His works.
[QURTUBI-FULL:43:9/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The polytheists acknowledge God created and brought the heavens and earth into existence, yet in ignorance worship others alongside Him.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The attributes may be implicit in what they say, supplying its content: as elsewhere, they effectively say “God.”
[BAYDAWI-FULL:43:6-10/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Alternatively, “the Mighty, Knowing” is their actual answer and the following description begins a new sentence.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#6/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | When asked, the polytheists acknowledge that the Mighty, All-Knowing One created the heavens and earth.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · أبو حاتم | reports | There is no pause at al-ʿAlīm because alladhī qualifies it; Abū Ḥātim allows a pause by supplying huwa before alladhī.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The reported answer that the Mighty, Knowing One created the heavens and earth is the people's own phrasing; their saying elsewhere that Allah created them does not rule out this answer.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Repeating خلقهن العزيز العليم in the answer intensifies emphasis; elsewhere they use Allah, the comprehensive name for the supreme attributes.

[SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The verb is repeated for emphasis: an answer to “Who stood?” could simply be “Zayd,” but the fuller verb is stated here.

[SAMIN-DURR:43:9/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The answer matches the question in meaning; matching its syntax would instead produce a nominal sentence.

[BURHAN:v4p48/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The wording explicitly says the heavens were created because the opponents appeared to be materialists or deniers who needed their creation stated outright.

[BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Although the direct answer could have been Allah, the answer repeats the verb خلق to match the question semantically and stress their admission, intensifying their rebuke.
[BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The Creator’s names entail that he overcomes everything and is overcome by nothing, and that his knowledge encompasses all things and his creative power is limitless.
[BIQAI-FULL:v7p8/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Arab idolaters admit that God created the cosmos while worshipping beings with no power or knowledge; their answer refutes their excuse and exposes deliberate obstinacy.
[ITQAN:v2p533/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | rejects | The answer الله in 43:87 is not a subject-less predicate beginning a sentence; it is the subject of the verb understood in the answer, as the parallel 43:9 wording shows. | mentions 43:87
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Man is an interrogative meaning who; the heavens and earth are the upper and lower cosmic bodies.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Quraysh acknowledge that the Mighty, Knowing one created the cosmos, yet their worship of others exposes human ignorance.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الإرشاد | reports | Al-Irshad says they truly attribute creation to one possessing these attributes, without necessarily using this exact title in their own wording.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | Another possibility is that these were Quraysh's actual words.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · فتح الرحمن | reports | Fath al-Rahman says the expected answer was simply that God created them; the Qur'an's wording introduces God's following attributes, distinct from the reported answer.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Primordial testimony at the covenant planted recognition of God's lordship and creation in human nature; only God's gracious attraction opens the way to His majesty.
[BURSEVI:v8p270#3/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The covenant's primordial affirmation bears fruit as people recognize God's creative power in this world. | mentions 7:172
[ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The question is coordinated with the preceding address; the verses beginning ‘How many messengers We sent’ interrupt to affirm the point and console the Prophet. | mentions 43:6
[ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says disbelievers attribute creation to God, who in reality has these attributes, without necessarily uttering the titles or consciously describing Him by them; Alusi accepts this as sufficient.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The prefatory oath lām, answer lām, and emphatic nūn ensure their answer, while treating an undisputed fact as debatable dramatizes their incoherence.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p167/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The staged question signals that they ignore God's creatorship in life and prayer: asked directly, they answer Allah at once, then return to shirk.

[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p169/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Verses 9–15 note the opponents' confession that the Powerful and Knowledgeable God created the heavens and earth, despite their assigning partners among His servants; the universe's signs support tawḥīd and the Day of Judgement.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:9/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The pagan Arabs did not regard their idols as equal to God in every quality; they admitted that creation belongs to God alone and requires great power and knowledge.

item.text: The main disagreements concern who “them” refers to, whether the divine titles are quoted words, and where the reported answer ends. I’m keeping those distinct from the shared point that the Meccan idolaters acknowledged God as creator.
